package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a high-severity Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs. This can be exploited to access internal resources, cause denial of service, or be chained with other vulnerabilities for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is present by default in affected versions and can be triggered without authentication.

execution_context.file_location: Core xmltooling library (C++), invoked by applications using OpenSAML/Shibboleth (e.g., shibd process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML snippet, when processed by the vulnerable xmltooling library, causes the application to fetch and process the external URI specified in the RetrievalMethod element. The library does not restrict the URI scheme or destination, allowing SSRF.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows untrusted XML input to specify arbitrary external URIs, which the application will fetch and process. This enables attackers to force the application to make network requests to internal or external resources, potentially exposing sensitive data or enabling further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, SAML/XML libraries should restrict or validate external resource loading to prevent SSRF. The vulnerable behavior allows arbitrary URI resolution from untrusted input, violating secure parsing expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may use RetrievalMethod to fetch keys from trusted, pre-configured locations, but should never allow arbitrary URIs from untrusted input.
key_indicators: Unrestricted URI resolution from XML input
No validation of URI scheme or destination
Network requests triggered by parsing attacker-supplied XML

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits malicious SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element with an attacker-controlled URI.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and fetches the external URI, resulting in SSRF.

attack_chain.action: The SSRF is used to access internal resources or trigger further vulnerabilities (e.g., chaining with command injection for RCE).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential unauthenticated remote code execution or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Parsing of SAML/XML input triggers outbound network requests to untrusted or unexpected destinations
Presence of KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external URIs in SAML/XML input
shibd or similar processes making HTTP/HTTPS requests during XML parsing
file_indicators: Unexpected or unlogged network activity from shibd or SAML-processing services
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled or non-whitelisted domains from SAML-processing hosts
Requests to internal resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata) triggered by SAML/XML parsing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML/XML parsing services (such as shibd) for outbound network requests during XML processing, especially those initiated by parsing KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements. Flag any SAML/XML input containing external URIs or unexpected URI schemes. Use network monitoring to detect requests to untrusted or internal destinations originating from SAML-processing applications. Patch xmltooling to v3.2.4+ or apply the BlockingXSECURIResolver fix to prevent exploitation.
